passage:
By lunch, the photo of Seema's clay volcano from the science fair had forty thousand views. Her phone buzzed against the desk like an insect, and each buzz made her chest bubble.
"Seema, you're famous! 🎉" Jomon said, grinning across the bench. She kept sneaking looks at the counter.
By evening it had slowed, and by night the number stood still. She felt a small dip and laughed at herself. "It was fun," she told Jomon on the walk home. "But I'm still the same person who hasn't finished her essay."
He laughed. That night she pinned a print of the volcano photo to her cupboard door and opened her notebook.

qa.q: What did Seema post that went viral?
qa.a: She posted a photo of her clay volcano from the science fair.

qa.q: What was Seema feeling with each buzz of the phone?
qa.a: Her chest bubbled with a rush of pride and excitement with every buzz. 😊

qa.q: How did Seema keep her worth separate from the numbers?
qa.a: She enjoyed it lightly, laughed at the dip when the counter stood still, and reminded herself she was still the same person with an essay to finish.

qa.q: How might Jomon see Seema's sudden fame?
qa.a: Jomon seems delighted for her and cheers her on, and her calm afterwards may show him that the number was never the point.

grounding: Shows a teen enjoying a viral post lightly without tying her worth to the numbers.

passage:
The network in Nani's village near Ratnagiri was one bar on a good day, and Parveen had exams in four days. But on Sunday afternoon she posted a short video of Nani rolling bhakris, singing an old Konkani song, flour on her nose.

By evening it had 40,000 views. By Monday, 200,000.

Parveen felt electric. She walked to the one spot near the well where the signal worked, again and again, refreshing. Comments from strangers: "Your Nani is precious!" "Made my day!" She skipped her revision to reply to them.

Her cousin Kavitha found her by the well at dusk. "Exams on Thursday, na?"

"I know. But look!"

"It's lovely. Nani is lovely." Kavitha paused. "But it'll drop next week. They always do."

Parveen felt a flicker of disappointment, then knew it was true. She took one screenshot to keep, showed Nani the kind comments, and walked back to the house. She left the phone on the shelf and opened her chemistry book.

qa.q: What was Nani doing in the video?
qa.a: Nani was rolling bhakris, singing an old Konkani song, with flour on her nose.

qa.q: What was Parveen feeling as the views climbed?
qa.a: Parveen felt an electric rush of excitement and pride, refreshing again and again.

qa.q: What did Parveen do that showed she was enjoying it lightly?
qa.a: Parveen kept one screenshot, shared the kind comments with Nani and went back to studying instead of chasing the numbers.

qa.q: How might Nani feel about the kind comments?
qa.a: Nani would likely feel touched and amused that strangers enjoyed her song and cooking.

grounding: It shows a teen whose post goes viral and gives her a rush, choosing to enjoy it lightly and not tie her worth to numbers that will drop.

passage:
Amandeep's meme about the school canteen samosa, drawn as a sad cartoon, went round the whole school in one day. Then round three other schools. By Wednesday it had 12,000 likes.

He couldn't stop smiling. Juniors pointed at him in the corridor. His phone buzzed every minute. For the first time, he felt like somebody.

On Friday he posted a second meme. He'd spent hours on it. It got 43 likes.

He checked it twenty times. His stomach sank each time. Was the first one just luck? Was he just ordinary again?

Sarika found him sitting on the steps near the canteen, scrolling his own old post. "You look like the sad samosa," she said.

He laughed, a bit. "The new one flopped."

"So? The first one was funny. You're still funny. The numbers don't decide that." She held out half her vada pav. "Draw something for the class magazine instead. People will keep that."

He took the vada pav. Later, he turned off like notifications.

qa.q: How many likes did Amandeep's second meme get?
What was Amandeep feeling when the second meme flopped?
qa.a: Amandeep felt disappointed and deflated, his stomach sinking, wondering if the first success was just luck.

qa.q: What did Sarika say that helped, and why?
qa.a: Sarika said the numbers don't decide whether he is funny and suggested drawing for the class magazine, which moves his worth away from likes.

qa.q: How does Sarika see Amandeep's flop?
qa.a: Sarika sees it as no big deal; she still thinks he is funny and wants him to make something that lasts, like a drawing for the magazine.

grounding: It shows a teen whose post goes viral and gives him a rush, learning to enjoy it lightly and not tie his worth to numbers that will drop.
